clue.text: Prepare to land a very quiet fish

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler readies to haul in a fish caught in near silence.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft making its final descent towards a runway is on its approach, so to prepare to land is this verb.

clue.text: Impressive summer days

explanation.surface: Grand weather in the middle of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: August means majestic and venerable; it is also the eighth month, part of the northern summer.

clue.text: What's page on South American chart turned up, perhaps?

definitions.text: What's page on South American chart turned up, perhaps?

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: a chart is a map

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a page of a South American map might show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses the run to give PAMPAS; 'on' simply sets page after South American. Read whole, the clue asks what such a chart shows: grassy plains.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast treeless grasslands of Argentina would appear on a map of South America.

clue.text: One, endlessly wanting edge in money gained could be?

definitions.text: One, endlessly wanting edge in money gained could be?

indicators.note: endlessly means the word one loses its last letter
in places the edge word inside the money word

parts.note: takings, money gained, is the take
a hem is an edge of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone always seeking an advantage in profit, it is suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves the first two letters of One; 'in' signals the container. The whole clue doubles as a portrait of a grasping opportunist chasing an edge in profits.
explanation.definitionFit: A person grasping for gain and advancement is said to be out for profit, an idiom for the self-seeking.

clue.text: To pepper, or when not to pepper pheasant?

parts.note: pushed to, as a door, means closed
to pepper food is to season it

explanation.surface: A cook wonders when to spice up a game bird, or whether not to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' as in a door pulled to means shut. 'Pepper' then switches sense: in the definition it means shoot with pellets, and pheasant may not be shot outside the open season.
explanation.definitionFit: The months when shooting a game bird is banned by law are its protected period.

clue.text: Jack's first course is difficult

explanation.surface: A sailor's first meal turns out to be hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Jack and Jill went up the hill, so the first course Jack took was this way; the phrase also means arduous.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack went up the hill in the rhyme, and a climbing task is a figure for a hard struggle.

clue.text: For Americans, quite the best book

parts.note: a plum job is the best one

explanation.surface: Americans say a certain book is quite the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage the word means completely, as in 'plumb crazy'.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang this adverb means utterly or completely, an intensifier like entirely.

clue.text: Old secret love affair — rueing it badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of rueing it are disordered

explanation.surface: Regret over a long-ago hidden romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges RUEING IT. The romance sense is dated, hence 'Old'.
explanation.definitionFit: This word once meant a clandestine amorous liaison; today it more often means plotting.

clue.text: Crowd abolishing franc, and, crowd suggesting end of pound?

indicators.note: abolishing means the franc's letter is removed from the crowd word

parts.note: a flock is a crowd
F is the abbreviation for franc
the gate at a match is the crowd attending

explanation.surface: Currency talk: ditching the franc, and fears about the end of the pound.
explanation.walkthrough: A canal pound is the stretch of water between locks, so the barrier at its end is this. 'abolishing' drops F from FLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound on a canal is a level reach closed at each end by a sluice barrier.

clue.text: Initiative outing MP is unfortunate

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests things gone awry, so the letters of outing MP are jumbled

explanation.surface: A politician being outed is an unlucky turn of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is unfortunate' rearranges OUTING and MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Initiative and resourcefulness are what this colloquial word for common sense and drive means.

clue.text: Simple game requiring short polo mallet

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: short means the word for the mallet loses its final letter

parts.note: a polo mallet is a stick

explanation.surface: A straightforward sport needs only a short mallet to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts STICK to STIC; RU is the usual crossword shorthand for rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic means plain and unsophisticated, like country life, so it serves as a synonym for simple.

clue.text: Communal rice in a paddy perhaps yielding no profit

indicators.note: a paddy is a temper, and rice in a temper is agitated, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Rice grown communally in a paddy field makes no money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a paddy perhaps' rearranges COMMUNAL RICE; paddy is British slang for a fit of temper as well as a rice field.
explanation.definitionFit: A venture that is not run for gain, or brings none, lacks a trading or business aim.

clue.text: Store stocking old Italian wine

indicators.note: stocking means holding within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to store is to save

explanation.surface: A shop keeps vintage bottles from Italy in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' puts O inside SAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white wine from the Veneto region of Italy.

clue.text: Putting up ones dukes?

parts.note: not raising fists for a fight but raising people to the peerage, making them dukes

explanation.surface: Squaring up with fists ready for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up your dukes' means raise your fists, but here the monarch is raising chosen people up to become dukes.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising someone to a peerage, such as a dukedom, is conferring nobility on them.

clue.text: Four pianists playing delicious item

indicators.note: playing hints at the letters of four pianists being performed in a new order

explanation.surface: A piano quartet gives a delightful performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges FOUR and PIANISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit of the passion flower vine is a tasty tropical food item.

clue.text: Grotesque fat cats in trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the letters of fat cats in are shaken up

explanation.surface: Overpaid bosses in difficulty make a hideous sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges FAT CATS IN; 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic in its older sense means bizarre and fanciful, much like weird or monstrous.

clue.text: Two things that may accompany bill for help with footwear

parts.words: Two things that may accompany bill
parts.note: the shoebill is a large African stork

parts.words: Two things that may accompany bill
parts.note: the hornbill is a tropical bird with a large beak

explanation.surface: Two items might come with an invoice for a shoe-fitting aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' is a bird's beak, not an invoice: both words join it to make a bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved spoon-like tool eases a heel into a tight boot or slipper.

clue.text: Venetian blind may need this, but not looking from street

definitions.text: Venetian blind may need this, but not looking from street

parts.words: Venetian blind may need this, but not looking from street
parts.note: read as a sightless person from Venice, not a slatted window shade seen from outside

explanation.surface: A slatted window shade needs something, though not for privacy from passers-by.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a window fitting; the cryptic reading is a citizen of Venice who cannot see and needs a trained animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained canine leads a sightless person safely about the streets.

clue.text: Gathering conflict between two sorts of dynasty

indicators.note: between means the conflict word sits inside, flanked by the two dynasties

parts.note: a royal house, such as the House of Windsor, is a dynasty
the Ming were a Chinese dynasty
war is conflict

explanation.surface: A war breaks out between two ruling families.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' signals the container; the definition sounds like any gathering but is a party in a new home.
explanation.definitionFit: A party held to celebrate moving into a new home is a social gathering.

clue.text: See you once in our embrace? One might have done

parts.note: V, from Latin vide, means see

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed within another
embrace means the word our wraps around the other piece

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of you

explanation.surface: Was the old-fashioned 'you' taken into our hug? Someone may have watched it happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'embrace' together signal the container, which builds OYEUR. The definition reads 'done' as 'seen', echoing the clue's opening verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeping Tom is one who has watched, so someone who might have looked on is this kind of watcher.

clue.text: Improves on identification for plant pest

parts.note: to cap something is to better it

explanation.surface: Better identification is needed for a garden pest.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsid is a sap-sucking bug that damages crops and garden plants.

clue.text: Serious attempt to nominate Inspector Morse?

explanation.surface: A determined bid to name the fictional detective.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse, the Oxford detective of novel and television, was revealed to have this rare first name, so to name him is to say it.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest effort is an endeavour; and Morse's given name in Colin Dexter's novels is the same word.

clue.text: A king in fear must be vigilant

indicators.note: in means the two pieces go inside the fear word

parts.note: awe is reverential fear
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A frightened monarch must stay on guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and K inside AWE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and watchful means not asleep, the opposite of dozing.

clue.text: In Figaro, Marcellina's part shows a subtle quality

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit within the words that follow
part means only a portion of these words is taken

explanation.surface: In Mozart's opera, a supporting soprano's role has something delicate about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcellina is a character in Mozart's The Marriage of Figaro, which sells the surface about an opera role.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrance, or a faint pervasive air about something, is a subtle quality.

clue.text: Something out of date worn by Dolly Varden perhaps?

explanation.surface: An unfashionable item a Dickens heroine might have put on.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolly Varden is a character in Dickens's Barnaby Rudge who gave her name to a broad flowered bonnet, a period headpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale and unoriginal is this idiom's sense; and a Dolly Varden bonnet is literally antique headgear.

clue.text: Fancy woman showing motorway nerves

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, read as MI
nerves means anxiety or stress

explanation.surface: A glamorous woman is jittery about driving on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy woman is old slang for a man's lover, a kept paramour.

clue.text: Clementine's relative sought for this fruit filled with egg flip?

indicators.note: filled with means the fruit word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a nut is a fruit

indicators.note: flip means the word egg is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fruit stuffed with a frothy egg drink, linked to the girl in the song.
explanation.walkthrough: In the song 'Oh My Darling, Clementine' her father was a forty-niner miner hunting gold. 'flip' makes GGE and 'filled with' signals the container; egg flip is also a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold rush miner like Clementine's father panned for lumps of gold.

clue.text: Crown servant given some stick in Parliament?

explanation.surface: A royal official gets a hard time in the House.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Rod is the House of Lords official who summons MPs at the State Opening, carrying an ebony staff; 'given some stick' also means criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gentleman Usher of this title is a royal officer, and his ebony staff is literally a dark stick used in Parliament.
